## `mf`

mind-forge: a local-first knowledge management CLI

**Usage:** `mf [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]`

###### **Subcommands:**

* `init` — Initialize a directory as a Mind Repo
* `project` — Manage projects
* `article` — Manage legacy articles
* `mind` — Manage minds, including minds without outputs
* `additional` — Discover and manage additional files and directories
* `lifecycle` — Apply and recover local layout lifecycle transactions
* `output` — Manage editable outputs belonging to minds
* `prompt` — View prompt projections
* `thinking` — View thinking projections
* `source` — Manage content sources
* `search` — Search the repository-wide RAG corpus
* `asset` — Manage project assets
* `term` — Manage terminology
* `build` — Build a selected mind output or legacy article
* `publish` — Publish selected outputs or legacy articles to configured targets
* `render` — Generate render prompts (emits prompts only, no output files)
* `config` — Manage configuration
* `completion` — Generate shell completion scripts
* `version` — Show version information

###### **Options:**

* `--root <PATH>` — Mind Repo root directory
* `--config <PATH>` — Config file path
* `-v`, `--verbose` — Verbose output
* `-q`, `--quiet` — Silence non-error output
* `-o`, `--output <FORMAT>` — Output format

  Default value: `text`

  Possible values: `text`, `json`

* `--json` — Shorthand for --output json
* `--no-color` — Disable colored output
* `-p`, `--project <NAME_OR_PATH>` — Project name or path (cwd-relative, repo-relative, or absolute)



## `mf init`

Initialize a directory as a Mind Repo

**Usage:** `mf init [PATH]`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<PATH>` — Target directory path (defaults to current directory)



## `mf project`

Manage projects

**Usage:** `mf project [COMMAND]`

###### **Subcommands:**

* `new` — Create a project
* `list` — List projects
* `archive` — Archive a project
* `lint` — Lint a project
* `index` — Index projects
* `show` — Show project details
* `update` — Update project metadata
* `import` — Import a directory as a project
* `rename` — Rename a project
* `remove` — Remove a project



## `mf project new`

Create a project

**Usage:** `mf project new [OPTIONS] <PATH>`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<PATH>` — Project path (cwd-relative, repo-relative, or simple name)

###### **Options:**

* `--layout <LAYOUT>` — Content layout for a new mind/output project

  Possible values: `category`, `bundle`

* `--template <TEMPLATE>`
* `-f`, `--force` — Proceed despite safety checks: overwrite an existing target, or remove an entity referenced by others
* `-n`, `--dry-run` — Preview changes without writing

###### **Options:**

## `mf project lint`

Lint a project

**Usage:** `mf project lint [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--fix` — Auto-fix issues that have a fixer
* `--rule <RULE>` — Restrict to a specific lint rule kind
* `--severity <LEVEL>` — Only emit issues at or above this severity (error|warning|info)
* `--max-warnings <N>` — Exit 1 when warnings exceed this count
* `-n`, `--dry-run` — Preview fixes without writing (only with --fix)
* `--include-suggested` — Apply all corrections including suggested
* `--min-confidence <0.0..1.0>` — Apply suggested corrections at or above this confidence

## `mf article new`

Create an article

**Usage:** `mf article new [OPTIONS] <TITLE>`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<TITLE>` — Article title (sole positional)

###### **Options:**

* `--slug <SLUG>` — Optional ASCII-friendly filename slug. Without it the title is used
* `-t`, `--template <TEMPLATE>` — Template: built-in schema name (blank/arch/prd/blog) or path under project root. Default: blank

  Default value: `blank`
* `--file` [alias: `single-file`] — Write a single file instead of a directory

  Default value: `false`
* `--tag <TAG>`
* `--draft`

  Default value: `true`
* `-f`, `--force` — Proceed despite safety checks: overwrite an existing target, or remove an entity referenced by others
* `-n`, `--dry-run` — Preview changes without writing

## `mf article convert`

Convert article shape between directory and single-file

**Usage:** `mf article convert [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--to-single-file` — Convert directory articles to single-file articles
* `--to-directory` — Convert single-file articles to directory articles
* `--merge` — Allow `--to-single-file` to merge multi-block directory articles (concatenated in filename order) instead of skipping them
* `--article <ARTICLE>` — Convert only this article (selector: bare slug, docs/<slug>, docs/<slug>.md, or exact title). Without it, converts every eligible article in the project (existing batch behaviour, unchanged)
* `-n`, `--dry-run` — Preview changes without writing

## `mf lifecycle`

Apply and recover local layout lifecycle transactions

**Usage:** `mf lifecycle <COMMAND>`

###### **Subcommands:**

* `convert` — Convert every output, core role, and owned additional resource
* `mind-rename` —
* `mind-move` —
* `mind-remove` —
* `output-rename` —
* `output-move` —
* `output-remove` —
* `apply` — Apply a saved hash-bound plan after revalidating its complete inventory
* `resume` — Resume an interrupted transaction or safely abort unpublished partial preparation
* `rollback` — Restore backed-up content, refusing to overwrite subsequent edits
* `status` — Inspect the current transaction without writing

## `mf source new`

Create a source

**Usage:** `mf source new [OPTIONS] <INPUT>`

###### **Arguments:**

###### **Options:**

* `--name <NAME>` — Override the source name derived from the input
* `--file-kind <FILE_KIND>` — File kind (mf primary). Use --source-kind for mind channel type

  Possible values: `auto`, `pdf`, `file`, `rss`, `web`

* `--source-kind <SOURCE_KIND>` — Source channel type (mind primary)

  Possible values: `yuque`, `meeting`, `misc`

* `--link` — Create a symlink instead of copying a local file
* `--register-only` — Register a file already inside the project's sources directory without copying it
* `--no-index` — Register only, without indexing the source into RAG (Lance backend). By default a new source is chunked and embedded so it is searchable at once
* `--article <ARTICLE>` — Originating article that introduced this source (project-relative path). Captured as authoritative import provenance (spec 071). Must stay within the project; an escaping path is a usage error
* `-f`, `--force` — Proceed despite safety checks: overwrite an existing target, or remove an entity referenced by others
* `-n`, `--dry-run` — Preview changes without writing

## `mf source search`

###### **Options:**

  Possible values: `basic`, `advanced`, `both`

* `-p`, `--project <NAME_OR_PATH>` — Limit search to a project name or path (cwd-relative, repo-relative, or absolute)
* `--file-kind <FILE_KIND>` — Filter by file kind
* `--source <SOURCE>` — Filter by source identity
* `--label <KEY=VALUE>` — Filter by label, `key=value` (repeatable; all must match)
* `--revision <REV>` — Search a specific content revision instead of the current version. Accepts an integer revision number, a date (2026-07-25), or a relative date (yesterday, "7 days ago")
* `--limit <LIMIT>` — Maximum results to return

  Default value: `20`

* `--source <SOURCE>` — Limit sync to a specific Source identity (requires unambiguous scope)
* `--offline` — Forbid all network access (Web/RSS acquisition disabled)
* `--rebuild` — Regenerate the Lance Source index to the current storage schema (full re-index/re-embed). Recovers from a schema-drift refusal in one command family instead of detouring to `source admin rebuild`
* `-n`, `--dry-run` — Preview changes without writing

## `mf term lint`

Lint term consistency in project docs

**Usage:** `mf term lint [OPTIONS] [PATH]`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<PATH>`

###### **Options:**

* `--article <ARTICLE>` — Target a specific article by slug or title
* `--term <NAME>` — Only apply/scan corrections for the named term(s) (repeatable, exact name)
* `--exclude-term <NAME>` — Exclude corrections for the named term(s) (repeatable)
* `--exclude-original <ORIGINAL>` — Exclude this exact original text across terms (repeatable)
* `--include-quotes` — Scan quoted text and blockquotes as well as ordinary prose
* `--ad-hoc <ORIGINAL=>CORRECT>` — Apply an invocation-only correction (repeatable): ORIGINAL=>CORRECT
* `--ad-hoc-from <PATH>` — Read invocation-only corrections, one ORIGINAL=>CORRECT per line
* `--fix` — Auto-fix issues that have a fixer
* `--rule <RULE>` — Restrict to a specific lint rule kind
* `--severity <LEVEL>` — Only emit issues at or above this severity (error|warning|info)
* `--max-warnings <N>` — Exit 1 when warnings exceed this count
* `-n`, `--dry-run` — Preview fixes without writing (only with --fix)
* `--include-suggested` — Apply all corrections including suggested
* `--min-confidence <0.0..1.0>` — Apply suggested corrections at or above this confidence
* `-y`, `--yes` — Skip interactive confirmation prompt

* `--confidence <CONFIDENCE>`
* `--clear-confidence`
* `--alias <ALIAS>`
* `--tag <TAG>`
* `--delete-alias <DELETE_ALIAS>` — Remove an alias from the term
* `--delete-tag <DELETE_TAG>` — Remove a tag from the term
* `--add-correction <ORIGINAL[:CORRECT]>` — Append a correction (ORIGINAL[:CORRECT]); defaults to word/required, term name as CORRECT
* `--correction-match <ORIGINAL:KIND>` — Set match kind of a correction: ORIGINAL:word|substring|pinyin
* `--correction-fix <ORIGINAL:KIND>` — Set fix kind of a correction: ORIGINAL:required|suggested
* `--correction-pinyin <ORIGINAL:PINYIN>` — Set pinyin of a correction: ORIGINAL:PINYIN
* `--delete-correction <DELETE_CORRECTION>` — Delete a correction by ORIGINAL
* `-n`, `--dry-run` — Preview changes without writing
